steps.text: Place butter, brown sugar, garlic, lemon juice, soy sauce, and pepper in a small saucepan. Warm over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until sugar is completely dissolved.

Lightly oil grill grate. Brush fish with brown sugar sauce, and place on grill. Cook for 5 minutes per side, or until fish can be easily flaked with a fork, basting with sauce. Discard remaining basting sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Barbeque Halibut Steaks
raw_recipe.description: A simple recipe for barbecued halibut. Soy sauce and brown sugar add a special zip that is uncommonly delicious.
raw_recipe.name: Barbeque Halibut Steaks

recipeInstructions.text: Place butter, brown sugar, garlic, lemon juice, soy sauce, and pepper in a small saucepan. Warm over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until sugar is completely dissolved.

Lightly oil grill grate. Brush fish with brown sugar sauce, and place on grill. Cook for 5 minutes per side, or until fish can be easily flaked with a fork, basting with sauce. Discard remaining basting sauce.

review.reviewBody: Yummy!! I used halibut steaks (3 steaks about 1.75 lbs total) and marinated them for a couple of hours. I changed the marinade just a little - first of all I doubled it, and I used olive oil instead of butter. I also used honey instead of brown sugar and added a couple of extra garlic cloves. I used the garlic press instead of a knife for the garlic because I like the way pressed garlic works in a marinade. I grilled my halibut on a stovetop grill, 5 minutes on the first side and 4 on the second, and I boiled the leftover marinade to drizzle over the fish on the plate. We loved it and I will make it again. I'll probably use this marinade on a slightly less expensive fish - here in NY the halibut cost $15.99 lb, so, it was a bit pricey. But what a gorgeous fish steak! Thanks.

OMG! I have made it twice loved it even more the second time! I changed it a bit the second time around and not only doubled the sauce ingredients, but added way more garlic (5 minced cloves). I marinated it for a few hours and added a sprinkle of extra brown sugar over the top after pouring the warm sauce over the steaks. I used aluminum foil instead of putting it directly on the grill. (I curled the edges up so the juice would not drip out) I did not waste any of the delicious sauce and added every drop to the foil. I also added some capers once it was on the grill (which added another WOW factor!) The steaks and capers cooked in the sizzling juices ~ the flavor was absolutely amazing. There was no fish taste and the garlic was subtle. I served the halibut steaks over a bed of fresh spinach leaves along with some saffron rice and a side of crab legs. The halibut was even better than the crab!!! I am in Alaska and friends are always bringing me fresh halibut, so I will make this recipe again and again!

I made this recipe, and made it with honey instead of brown sugar. I also added fresh ginger, minced and err on the side of more garlic. I marinated it for 30 minutes, it tastes a bit like a Teriyaki marinate. I started with a very hot pan and seared each side one minute to score each side. I then put it in the oven at 350 degrees for 10 more minutes. Delicious!!! I will make this again. Thank you!

This had to be one of the easiest recipes I have made in years. I used the sauce to quickly marinate the fish while the grill was getting hot (about 10 minutes). I also didn’t grill the fish directly on the grill, but put it on a sheet of foil on the top rack at medium high heat. We had 4 large halibut fillets; skin on. Skin side down for 5 - 6 minutes and turned them for about 5 minutes to finish. End result was juicy flakey fish. Served with coleslaw an hot bread. Excellent and will be making this again.

AMAZING!!! I did this with a salmon filet and the fresh garlic cloves. Sooo unbelievably good! Good sweet and sour. It was easy and packed quite a zippy punch! I baked it uncovered in my oven on 400 for 13 min after brushing the filet with the sauce and then pouring the remaining sauce in the Pyrex. I served it over rice that I drizzled with some of the sauce after it came out of the oven. This was better than anything I've had at a restaurant for a long time!!! New favorite!!

Incredible! The caramelization on the fish from the sauce was insane delicious. I marinated my halibut in the sauce for more than 4 hours then popped it in my fish grill basket and cooked over charcoal. Seriously, this was the best halibut I've ever eaten. I WILL keep this recipe handy for future uses...like every use. Thanks a gazillion for sharing it!

Delicious and easy! I doubled the recipe and used 3 tablespoons of lemon juice. Brushed some of the maringade on 30 minutes before cooking. Grilled it on hardwood charcoal with a few applewood chips. Even my husband who doesn't like fish liked it.

i love this recipe. we usally dont have halibut in the house but we had it given to us. when i made it pretty much quadrupled the recipe because i looked at the recipe and i knew that it wouldn't work for even 1 pound of halibut when i was useing 2. even after doing extra on everything i put in some more suger but not more then another 2 tablespoons and a whole stick of butter total. plus i added a lot more garlic, some onions(i love both), and sesame seeds (they go good with anything). my grill ran out of propane but i didn't realize that until after i had already made the dish so i decided to broil it at 500 degrees. i had a shallow broiling pan with a grill slited lid. i put a thin grill thats supposed to be used for cooling cookies on top and i had a grill. for the sauce i did use the sauce pan but i didn't have a basting brush so i stuck the halibut in the pan for about 30 seconds each side before broiling. then before broiling i ran all the sauce over the halibut and scooped the onions, crushed garlic, and sesame seeds on top. it worked out really well because the broil cooked all sides at once and made the onions, garlic, and sesame seeds crispy and carmelized. also the brown suger crystalized on top and all over the halibut slices that is had cut the filet into (roughly 2"x 2"x 6"). overall i love the recipe with my adjustments, and i encourage others to modify recipes and experiment with things you like because eventually you will make it better.

This recipe is a good one... the only thing about it is, instead of using butter, i used Extra-Virgin Olive oil, and i reduced the amount of soy sauce by a teaspoon, and added a bit of honey to the mix.I also marinated the fish for about an hour or so b4 baking as it was too cold to grill outside, and i didnt feel like using my indoor on-stove grill. Needless to say there was nothing left and even my 7 yr old(the pickiest eater) liked it! Delicious! WIll use it again, and with other fish!

Delicious! I doubled the recipe for 1.25 lbs of fresh Halibut. I used half to marinade for an hour or so and saved the remaining for basting. I grilled each side for about 4-minutes on medium-high and served immediately. I'll definitely make this again.
Excellent, everyone loved it. Would be good for company. Baked it at 350 for about 20 minutes, didn't grill.

This is an excellent recipe not only for halibut, but for any white fish. I generally marinate the fish for an hour before barbequing or baking the fish in the oven or air fryer. Having been using this recipe for a few years.
My whole family enjoyed this marinade. We made extra to add to plain brown rice served alongside the grilled fish.
I have used this recipe for several years and have put it on chicken and salmon as well. Absolutely love it! So good

This was delicious on grilled halibut. I will definitely use this recipe again. The whole family was very impressed with flavor. It isn’t too strong for the halibut, which was my only concern. Perfect!!!
Tasty however salty: try a lower sodium soy sauce...

Very good: I was skeptical about the marinade but to my surprise my wife and I loved it !!!
I smoked mine at 400f and pulled it off at 129f. It took about 20 minutes. Will definitely make it again.
Followed the enhanced process in “rainstripe”’s review below and also added cayenne and fresh ginger. Big hit with even the non-fish lovers in my family.
